questions.prompt: Fixed costs 800 dollars, price 20 dollars, variable cost 10 dollars. What is break-even?
questions.intro: The BREAK-EVEN point is the number of sales at which total revenue equals total cost, so profit is zero. Each sale contributes (price - variable cost per item) toward fixed costs. Break-even units = fixed costs / (price - variable cost). Example (assumptions): fixed costs 600 dollars a month, price 15 dollars, variable cost 5 dollars: 600 / 10 = 60 sales. Sales above break-even create profit; sales below create a loss. Write down the assumptions; if any change, recalculate. Round UP, because you cannot sell part of an item.

questions.prompt: What is 300 / 7, rounded up?
questions.intro: Break-even is a division: fixed costs divided by contribution per sale. If the answer is not a whole number, round UP to the next whole number, because a partial sale is not possible and rounding down would leave you short. Example: 250 / 6 = 41.67, so 42 sales. Check: 42 x 6 = 252, which covers 250; 41 x 6 = 246, which does not.
